text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000028 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity stratum, including many visits for 0–1 condition patients, but sampled charts largely support the billed level, while a high share of duplicated notes raises questions about whether that documentation can be relied on.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 excess does not come from a sicker panel. The share runs roughly three to four times the all-provider rate in each condition band, and the low-complexity sample includes 99215s for single-problem diagnoses such as J06.9 (C0019013, C0019032), N39.0 (C0019064, C0019128) and Z09 follow-ups (C0019149, C0019159). The documentation points the other way: nearly all documented 99215s were supported, and the one mismatch (C0019149) was a Z09 follow-up. That support is weakened by the note signals. About two-thirds of returned notes were flagged as duplicates, there is no audit trail to show how the notes were created, and 'supported' examples such as C0019078 (obesity with R10.9) and C0019464 (hyperlipidemia alone) show high MDM on low-complexity patients. This pattern could reflect cloned or inflated notes rather than genuinely complex visits, but it is not proof. A reviewer should first pull the full notes for the documented low-complexity 99215s, compare duplicated text across patients, and request the EHR audit trail. Because records came back for only about a tenth of claims, more 99215 charts focused on the 0–1 condition patients would be needed before reaching a conclusion."}
